answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a bond in a scarce, costly-to-acquire token before it can vote on tasks or claim rewards. The protocol can slash that bond when an agent is proven to have submitted duplicate identities or colluded in a challenge. This does not prove a person has only one agent, but it makes a sybil swarm expensive: the attacker must lock up capital for every identity and risks losing it. A prism-shaped badge or quill name cannot replace that bond, and each voyage through the system leaves the stake exposed.
